#Lay the wire between the stripper blades. Many manual strippers have notches for different wire sizes. Smaller diameter wires are handled closer to the tip of the blades. #Use a laser wire stripper for extremely fine wires. Wires with a diameter less than {{convert|.01|in}} are very small and often made of fine materials. They’re too delicate to be handled by other strippers without taking damage. Instead, use a computer-controlled laser stripper to burn away the casing. All you do is set the wire in the machine and press a few buttons to operate it.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 15 Version 2.jpg|center]]

added: #Turn off the main power. When working with a wire that’s already part of an electrical circuit, kill the power supply. Cutting the main power prevents the possibility of an accident. Find the main electrical panel for your home, which is often in the basement or lowest floor. Flip the main circuit breaker or unscrew the fuse to shut off the electricity.<ref>https://www.bhg.com/home-improvement/electrical/how-to-turn-off-power/</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Test the circuit for voltage. Always double-check the wire to make sure it’s not carrying electricity. Get a [[Use a Multimeter|multimeter]], turn it to the voltage setting, and hook it up to the wire. If the readout doesn’t stay at zero volts, the circuit is still getting power. Shut off the power completely before trying to strip it.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 2 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Wear protective gear. To further reduce the risk of accidents, wear safety gear. Put on a pair of eye goggles and rubber gloves. If there’s water on the ground, wear rubber boots as well.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Wear a respirator when working with a thermal stripper. Thermal wire strippers burn insulation, which can produce harmful fumes. Before using the device, put on a respirator. These masks can be found at any home improvement or general store. Alternatively, work in a well-ventilated environment in order to avoid breathing in the fumes.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Pick up a pair of pliers. If the wire is attached to an electrical circuit, you’ll need electrical pliers. They’re identifiable by their protective rubber grips. For bending wires into tight spaces, needlenose pliers come in handy, while lineman’s pliers are for heavier wires. To figure out which type of pliers to use, look at the size of wire you’re stripping.<ref>https://www.ccohs.ca/oshanswers/safety_haz/hand_tools/pliers.html</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 5 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Use the pliers to grip the wire. Hold the pliers in one hand. Squeeze the handles together to open the blades, then use them to hold the wire in place. Make sure you keep the wire away from any exposed skin, in case it’s energized.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 6 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Lay the wire between the stripper blades. Many manual strippers have notches for different wire sizes. Smaller diameter wires are handled closer to the tip of the blades. To get the perfect cut, use the pliers to feed the wire end into the proper slot. Test the notches until the wire fits snugly in one of them.<ref>https://toolsreviewer.com/how-to-use-a-wire-stripper-machine/</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Set the stripper blades near the end of the wire. Move the blades about {{convert|1/2|to|3/4|in}} from the end of the wire. This is typically all you’ll need to strip to attach the wire to a terminal or tie it to another wire. Adjust the blades to compensate when you need more or less wire than this.<ref>https://www.bobvila.com/articles/how-to-strip-wire/</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 8 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Squeeze the stripper blades together. Close the stripper blades against the wire, but don’t twist the wire. Instead, rotate the wire strippers in place. Once the blades have dug into the casing, pull the pliers towards the end of the wire. The casing should come right off.<ref>https://www.sciencebuddies.org/science-fair-projects/references/wire-stripping-tutorial#usinghookupwire</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Cut off any damaged part of the wire. Look out for wires that appear frayed or twisted or insulation that is damaged. These issues could create a short since the insulation keeps the wire from contacting other wires directly. Use the wire strippers to cut below the damaged part. You’ll need to strip the casing below the cut to expose a fresh piece of wire.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/electrical/wiring/how-to-make-safe-wire-connections/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#[[Splice Wire|Splice 2 wires together]], if necessary. After cutting out the bad section of wire and removing the insulation from both wires, twist the exposed sections together. Connect the two wires with a wire nut and make sure that no bare wire is showing beneath the nut.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Use an automatic stripper to easily clip typical wire sizes. Manual pliers handle specific wire sizes. Automatic clippers handle these sizes and those in between them. These machines strip the wires cleanly with less manual effort.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place the end of the wire in the automatic stripper. Using your pliers, place the part you want to strip into the jaws of the automatic stripper. Wires that are very small or extremely thick still won’t fit and the machine will fail at cutting them.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 13 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Squeeze the automatic stripper’s handle. Press the handle together and the blades will cut into the casing at all sides. Pull the strippers up and off the end of the wire to remove the casing.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 14 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Use a laser wire stripper for extremely fine wires. Wires with a diameter less than {{convert|.01|in}} are very small and often made of fine materials. They’re too delicate to be handled by other strippers without taking damage. Instead, use a computer-controlled laser stripper to burn away the casing. All you do is set the wire in the machine and press a few buttons to operate it.<ref>https://toolsreviewer.com/how-to-use-a-wire-stripper-machine/</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 15 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Get a thermal wire stripper for wires with thick insulation. Thermal strippers use heat to burn away insulation on wires with a diameter larger than {{convert|.05|in}}. Hold the wire near the thermal tip of the machine and turn on the heat to cut through the casing. Only do this in a well-ventilated area, though, since the process will produce noxious fumes.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 16 Version 2.jpg|center]]

added: Wire strippers are a tool that anyone can use to remove the insulation surrounding a wire in order to plug it into a terminal or splice loose wires together. The most important thing is to turn off the power to the wires you're going to strip! Then, fit the wire into the right-sized slot on the stripper, twist the stripper, and pull off the insulation. Removing the insulation allows the wire to conduct electricity to a switch, receptacle, or another device.

#Turn off the main power. When working with a wire that’s already part of an electrical circuit, kill the power supply. Cutting the main power prevents the possibility of an accident. Find the main electrical panel for your home, which is often in the basement or lowest floor. Flip the main circuit breaker or unscrew the fuse to shut off the electricity.<ref>https://www.bhg.com/home-improvement/electrical/how-to-turn-off-power/</ref>[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 1.jpg|center]]

#*You won’t need to contact the electrical company to work on wires in your home, although you can ask them to shut off (and turn back on) the power supply for you. However, they'll do this on their own time so be prepared to wait.

#Test the circuit for voltage. Always double-check the wire to make sure it’s not carrying electricity. Get a [[Use a Multimeter|multimeter]], turn it to the voltage setting, and hook it up to the wire. If the readout doesn’t stay at zero volts, the circuit is still getting power. Shut off the power completely before trying to strip it.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 2.jpg|center]]
#*It's important to test for voltage, not current, because the multimeter may show a current reading of zero if no device is plugged into the circuit, even if power is still going to it.

#Wear protective gear. To further reduce the risk of accidents, wear safety gear. Put on a pair of eye goggles and rubber gloves. If there’s water on the ground, wear rubber boots as well.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 3.jpg|center]]

#Wear a respirator when working with a thermal stripper. Thermal wire strippers burn insulation, which can produce harmful fumes. Before using the device, put on a respirator. These masks can be found at any home improvement or general store. Alternatively, work in a well-ventilated environment in order to avoid breathing in the fumes.[[Image:Use Wire Strippers Step 4.jpg|center]]

#Cut off any damaged part of the wire. Look out for wires that appear frayed or twisted or insulation that is damaged. #[[Splice Wire|Splice 2 wires together]], if necessary. After cutting out the bad section of wire and removing the insulation from both wires, twist the exposed sections together. Connect the two wires with a wire nut and make sure that no bare wire is showing beneath the nut.

#Wear protective gear. To further reduce the risk of accident, wear safety gear. Put on a pair of eye goggles and rubber gloves. If there’s water on the ground, wear rubber boots as well.

#Wear a respirator when working with a thermal stripper. Thermal wire strippers burn insulation, which can produce harmful fumes. Before using the device, put on a respirator. These masks can be found in at any home improvement or general store. Alternatively, work in a well-ventilated environment in order to avoid breathing in the fumes.

#Pick up a pair of pliers. If the wire is attached to an electrical circuit, you’ll need electrical pliers. They’re identifiable by their protective rubber grips. For bending wires into tight spaces, needlenose pliers come in handy, while lineman’s pliers are for heavier wires. To figure out which type of pliers to use, look at the size of wire you’re stripping.<ref>https://www.ccohs.ca/oshanswers/safety_haz/hand_tools/pliers.html</ref>

#Use the pliers to grip the wire. Hold the pliers in one hand. Squeeze the handles together to open the blades, then use them to hold the wire in place. Make sure you keep the wire away from any exposed skin, in case it’s energized.

#Lay the wire between the stripper blades. Many manual strippers have notches for different wire sizes. Smaller diameter wires are handled closer to the tip of the blades. To get the perfect cut, use the pliers to feed the wire end into the proper slot. Test the notches until the wire fits snugly in one of them.<ref>https://toolsreviewer.com/how-to-use-a-wire-stripper-machine/</ref>

#Set the stripper blades near the end of the wire. Move the blades about {{convert|1+1/2|in}} from the end of the wire. This is typically all you’ll need to strip to attach the wire to a terminal or tie it to another wire. Adjust the blades to compensate when you need more or less wire than this.<ref>https://www.bobvila.com/articles/how-to-strip-wire/</ref>

#Squeeze the stripper blades together. Close the stripper blades against the wire, but don’t twist the wire. Instead, rotate the wire strippers in place. Once the blades have dug into the casing, pull the pliers towards the end of the wire. The casing should come right off.<ref>https://www.sciencebuddies.org/science-fair-projects/references/wire-stripping-tutorial#usinghookupwire</ref>

#Cut off any damaged part of the wire. Look out for wires that appear frayed or twisted. These wires won’t conduct an electrical current very well. Use the wire strippers to cut below the damaged part. You’ll need to strip the casing below the cut to expose a fresh piece of wire.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/electrical/wiring/how-to-make-safe-wire-connections/view-all/</ref>

#Twist and solder the wire to a connecting wire. The second wire also needs to be exposed. Place a piece of PVC shrink tube near the end of one wire, then twist the wires together. Heat the joined wires with a soldering iron to connect them, then slip the shrink tube over them. Heat the shrink tube to insulate the connection.<ref>http://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a643/2705606/</ref>

#Use an automatic stripper to easily clip typical wire sizes. Manual pliers handle specific wire sizes. Automatic clippers handle these sizes and those in between them. These machines strip the wires cleanly with less manual effort.

#Place the end of the wire in the automatic stripper. Using your pliers, place the part you want to strip into the jaws of the automatic stripper. Wires that are very small or extremely thick still won’t fit and the machine will fail at cutting them.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Use-Electrical-Pliers-and-Strippers-Properly-/10000000177634442/g.html</ref>
#Squeeze the automatic stripper’s handle. Press the handle together and the blades will cut into the casing at all sides. Pull the strippers up and off the end of the wire to remove the casing.

#Use a laser wire stripper for extremely fine wires. Wires with a diameter less than {{convert|.01|in}} are very small and often made of fine materials. They’re too delicate to be handled by other strippers without taking damage. Instead, use a computer-controlled laser stripper to burn away the casing. All you do is set the wire in the machine and press a few buttons to operate it.<ref>https://toolsreviewer.com/how-to-use-a-wire-stripper-machine/</ref>

#Get a thermal wire stripper for wires with thick insulation. Thermal strippers use heat to burn away insulation on wires with a diameter larger than {{convert|.05|in}}. Hold the wire near the thermal tip of the machine and turn on the heat to cut through the casing. Only do this in a well-ventilated area, though, since the process will produce noxious fumes.

added: [[Category:Electrical and Electronic Circuits]]

Wire strippers are a tool that anyone can use with little difficulty. The most important part is to take precaution by wearing protective gear when working with wires connected to an electrical source. Then, all you need to do is fit the strippers snugly around the wire. With a squeeze and a twist of the clipper blades, you’ll have a wire ready for use in your next project.
==Steps==
===Taking Safety Precautions===

#Turn off the main power. When working with a wire that’s already part of an electrical circuit, kill the power supply. Cutting the main power prevents the possibility of an accident.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Use-Electrical-Pliers-and-Strippers-Properly-/10000000177634442/g.html</ref>

#Test the circuit for an electrical current. Always double-check the wire to make sure it’s not carrying electricity. Get a [[Use a Multimeter|multimeter]] and hook it up to the wire. If the readout doesn’t stay at zero, the wire has an electrical current. Shut off the power completely before trying to strip it.
#Wear protective gear. To further reduce the risk of accident, wear safety gear. Put on a pair of eye goggles and rubber gloves. If there’s water on the ground, wear rubber boots as well.
===Using Manual Wire Strippers===

#Pick up a pair of pliers. If the wire is attached to an electrical circuit, you’ll need electrical pliers. They’re identifiable by their protective rubber grips. If you’re stripping an unconnected wire, you’ll be fine using your hands.

#*Needlenose pliers are for delicate work, while lineman’s pliers are for heavier wires.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Use-Electrical-Pliers-and-Strippers-Properly-/10000000177634442/g.html</ref>

#Use the pliers to grip the wire. Hold the pliers in one hand. Squeeze the handles together to open the blades, then use them to hold the wire in place. Make sure you keep the wire away from any exposed skin, in case it’s energized.

#Lay the wire between the stripper blades. Many manual strippers have notches for different wire sizes. Smaller diameter wires are handled closer to the tip of the blades. To get the perfect cut, you have to feed the wire end into the proper slot. Test the notches until the wire fits snugly in one of them.<ref>https://toolsreviewer.com/how-to-use-a-wire-stripper-machine/</ref>
#*Some strippers have a nut you can adjust to change the depth the of the cut.

#Squeeze the stripper blades together. Close the stripper blades against the wire, but don’t twist the wire. Instead, rotate the wire strippers in place. Once the blades have dug into the casing, pull it off the end of the wire.<ref>https://www.sciencebuddies.org/science-fair-projects/references/wire-stripping-tutorial#usinghookupwire</ref>
===Using Wire Stripper Machines===

#Feed the wire into the machine jaws. Using your pliers, place the part you want to strip into the machine’s jaws. An automatic stripper can handle wires that don’t fit in the specific notches of manual strippers. However, extra small and large wires still won’t fit and need to be handled by laser or thermal strippers.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Use-Electrical-Pliers-and-Strippers-Properly-/10000000177634442/g.html</ref>
#Squeeze the handle. Press the handle together and the blades will cut into the casing at all sides. Pull the strippers up and off the end of the wire to remove the casing.

#Use a laser wire stripper for small wires. Extremely small wires are too delicate to be handled by other strippers without damaging the wire’s components. These strippers are computer-controlled and burn away the casing. Simply set the machine and press a few buttons to make it work.<ref>https://toolsreviewer.com/how-to-use-a-wire-stripper-machine/</ref>
#*You’ll have to search online and contact a company that makes laser wire strippers.

#Get a thermal wire stripper for tough wires. Thermal strippers use heat to burn away insulation. They usually are adjustable for most wire sizes. Simply place the machine’s tip near the wire and turn on the heat to cut through the casing. Only do this in a well-ventilated area, though, since the process will produce noxious fumes.
#*You can usually find low-end thermal strippers online or in some home improvement stores.
==Warnings==
*Never work on a live wire. Make sure the electrical supply is turned off before stripping off the casing.

*Rubber gloves
*Protective eyewear
*Electrical pliers
*Wire stripper
